title: Water-quality recovery moved English river fish toward cold-water species, but it hid only 1-7% of the expected warming signal in the fish temperature index, 1990-2025
abstract: Question: did recovery from organic pollution hide a warming signal in the community temperature index (CTI) of English river fish? An earlier campaign study found that this CTI did not follow local warming and did not model water quality. Approach: we joined 18,166 Environment Agency electric-fishing surveys at 2,165 sites (1990-2025) to WHPT ASPT, a biological water-quality score from independent invertebrate samples on the same water bodies, and to E-OBS air temperature. We wrote the test plan before the join. Results: across 25 species, the species water-quality index had a correlation of -0.60 (p = 0.002) with the species thermal index, so clean-water species are cold-water species. Within sites, with region-by-year effects, a 1-unit higher 3-year ASPT gave a CTI (without eel) 0.029 C lower (95% CI -0.051 to -0.006); a future-ASPT placebo had no effect. ASPT rose 0.12 units per decade and air temperature 0.26 C per decade. Four estimates of the hidden warming signal were 0.0035 to 0.0175 C per decade, 1.4% to 6.8% of the warming rate, all below the pre-set 0.05 C per decade level. The ASPT-adjusted CTI trend was +0.004 C per decade (1.5% of warming). At sites without ASPT change the CTI rose 0.025 C per decade (9% of warming). Thus water-quality recovery is a real but small reason for the missing fish thermophilization. Limitations: ASPT is a biological proxy, not chemistry; pairing ignores river direction; the species water-quality index comes from the same fish data; regional estimates are imprecise and the effect was not clear after 2008.

citations.reason: Found no fish CTI tracking of warming in English rivers and named water quality as untested; we use its survey selection and species thermal index and test the water-quality explanation.
Showed continued invertebrate shift to pollution-sensitive families in English rivers; we use the same EA invertebrate release as a water-quality exposure for fish.
Weak temporal transfer of temperature and BOD gradients in English river invertebrates; related evidence for slow community response.
